- How do you handle aggregation across rapid-fire short requests (50–200 token responses) vs. occasional long-context sessions (~8k tokens)? Do short bursts get rounded up to a per-call minimum, or are they aggregated into a rolling window?
- How is KV cache usage billed? If we have a long-lived chat session that restores a KV cache, does rehydration count as input tokens each time?
- Can you provide a one-page sample invoice that shows baseline charges + rounding/minimums + a small discount line? Our finance team needs a concrete example to compare with internal modeling.

Luke — thanks for the clear list. High level answers first, then I'll attach a short calculation sheet and a sample invoice. Marissa and Ben are looped in for pricing/contract detail.

Quick bullets:
- Billing unit: we meter per token with 1-token granularity. There is no hidden chunking, but we apply a short-window aggregation for minimums: requests that begin within a 45s conversation window are aggregated toward a single "conversation window" minimum. That reduces overcharging on back-to-back micro-interactions.
- Short bursts vs long sessions: short calls (sub-512 tokens) are eligible for a per-window minimum of 32 tokens by default on hosted plans; long-context calls bill actual tokens for input+output (no extra rounding beyond token granularity). For dedicated/committed agreements we can reduce the per-window minimum to 8–16 tokens or remove it entirely.
- KV cache: tokenization for the KV cache only bill when the content is transmitted as part of an API call (i.e., rehydrating a cache into a request counts the tokens included in that request). If you use persistent session pinning (Dedicated), we can optionally bill cached prefix tokens separately as a smaller "cache-read" charge that is discounted compared to live input tokens.

I've attached: redwood_calculation_examples.xlsx (worked examples using your attached CSV) and redwood_sample_invoice_Adeptive.pdf (one-page mock invoice).

Next steps: if you can confirm which committed tier you expect (1M, 5M, or 20M tokens / month), Marissa will put together a clear per-1M effective price after a discount and a proposal that reduces the minimums for the pilot.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Enterprise Sales (EMEA & US)
Redwood Inference

Hi Luke — looping in pricing details as requested. Short answers + formal proposal items below.

1) Effective per-1M price and minimums
- The "effective" per-1M price in our proposal assumes you take the committed tier discount and that short-window minimums are reduced (not waived) unless you select Dedicated capacity. Example (committed 5M / month): list = $50 / 1M tokens → 20% commit discount = $40 / 1M effective. Minimums reduction (32→12 tokens) is modeled into the example invoice as an adjustment line; net effect on the per-1M is <1.5% for your provided distribution.

2) Overages and burst handling
- Overage: billing uses committed rate for the first 20% above commitment (grace band) then tiered overage at list for remaining. We do not auto-throttle; we offer optional guardrail rules (rate limiting or fallback routing to smaller models) you can enable in the Console.

3) Cache-read treatment and invoicing
- Cache-reads appear as a separate line item. They are billed at a discounted rate (example: 10% of live input token rate) and are grouped per-session in the invoice so you can reconcile against session ids.

Attachments:
- Adeptive_proposal_v2.pdf (formal pricing + commitment language)
- redwood_calculation_examples.xlsx (updated with overage scenarios)

Pilot concession: we propose a 3-month pilot where we hard-cap your minimums to the reduced value (12 tokens) and provide a one-time invoice credit equal to estimated rounding exposure (~$750). After pilot, standard minimum policies apply unless you move to Dedicated.

If you sign the proposal I'll ask Legal to include the minimums reduction in the SOW. DocuSign in related links.

Best regards,
Marissa Cole
